response.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT r.name AS name, AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM per_name) SELECT AVG(p.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points, AVG(p.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(p.cnt - o.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM per_name p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.cnt > o.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Grouping is by races.name only (all years combined), so a race name like 'British Grand Prix' is one group across seasons.
The count is the number of driverStandings rows joined to a race under that name (COUNT(*) after inner join), including rows with NULL points; the average ignores NULL points via AVG.
The overall average count is the unweighted mean of per-name counts across all race names (before filtering).
Points are the season-to-date running totals as stored, averaged directly without any adjustment.
